keyFindings.description: The restarted reconcileWait after the repair races the bus's recovery backoff. recoverUntilHealthy waits 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 30 s between attempts (internal/bus/recovery.go:308-309, 363-369), and each attempt fails at once while the member is down, so attempts run at about t0, +1, +3, +7, +15, +31, +61. A repair that ends after t0+31 (Cluster.AwaitReady restarting the started member twice: muteAfter 15 s, muteRestarts 3, internal/testnats/cluster.go:156-163, 185-189; the implementer measured one AwaitReady in three restarting once) leaves the next attempt up to 30 s away while the new deadline is also 30 s away, so the Fatalf can fire just before the bus reconciles. The wait after a repair must cover reconcileWait plus the bus's 30 s maximum backoff, and the doc comment must stop claiming reconcileWait alone bounds the reconcile the repair makes possible.

The one-caller repair mode (nullable callback, one-shot latch, deadline reset, 10 doc lines) sits inside the wait five tests share, and refusedDispatchStream copies that wait's loop (reconciled check, deadline, fatal, sleep). Split into two single-purpose waits over connectDispatchStream's client (await the reconcile; await the first logged hook failure), so the new test reads connect, await failure, restart member, await reconcile on the test goroutine, and the settings_test.go:922 case reads connect, await failure, close. The code-quality pass built this on a scratch copy: vet clean, the affected tests pass, the file 31 lines shorter.

The HookedConnectionEvents() < 1 check cannot fail: the helper returns only under HookedConnectionEvents() >= 1, and hookedEvents never decreases (internal/bus/recovery.go:201-217). Delete it; the split above removes it anyway.

Fixed by the reviewer in 4430e212: both rows said Dispatch 'reconciles the stream on each connection'; ensureStreamOnce does nothing once one run has succeeded (internal/bus/nats.go:490-505), and the minute runs from the first uncovered connection event, which for Dispatch is its first connection (nats.go:584-589). The rows and the changelog fragment now say so.
